subject: SparkBridge: SDK onboarding sprint — throttles, backoff & endpoint migration
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Parker Lim <parker@sparkbridge.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SparkBridge: SDK onboarding sprint — throttles, backoff & endpoint migration

Hi Parker — great to meet you yesterday. Per our call I sketched a short onboarding sprint and a few technical guidelines to make your SDK integration with Redwood predictable across dev/sandbox/prod. Attaching a short quickstart and an action-plan spreadsheet.

High-level sprint (week 0 -> go-live):
- Week 0: sandbox creds + sample app test (we provide SDK sample).
- Week 1: migration to production endpoint behind feature flag; integration tests and telemetry.
- Week 2: cutover, ramp & mitigate (rate fencing and canary traffic).

Quick technical notes (copyable):
1) SDK install + auth (Python):
```python
pip install redwood-sdk
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="sk_live_...", base_url="https://api.redwood.ai/v1")
resp = client.generate("Summarize the page")
```
Node example:
```js
const {RedwoodClient} = require('redwood-sdk')
const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY })
await client.generate({ prompt: 'Hello' })
```
2) Endpoints & migration notes:
- Sandbox: https://sandbox.api.redwood.ai/v1 (no billing)
- Prod (hosted): https://api.redwood.ai/v1
- Dedicated (if you choose reserved capacity): https://dedicated-us.redwood.ai/v1 (region-specific hostnames)
Migration pattern: keep client configurable, add `REDWOOD_BASE_URL` env var and a feature-flag to flip from sandbox -> prod. Run integration tests with v1/health and a small probe before cutover.

3) Retries/Timeouts & idempotency:
- Client timeout: start with 10s for short generation calls; for large streaming jobs set 60s.
- Retries: up to 3 retries on 5xx and network errors with exponential backoff (base 500ms -> 500ms, 1s, 2s).
- Idempotency: include `Idempotency-Key` for non-idempotent operations if you retry POSTs that create resources.

4) Rate limit & backpressure guidance:
- Default hosted quota: 50 requests/sec per API key (bursts allowed up to 200 for short periods).
- For predictable throughput, implement token-bucket client-side with a burst window and average fill-rate matching your SLA.
- If you see 429s: reduce concurrency, implement jittered exponential backoff, and prefer batching multiple prompts per request where applicable.
- Recommended per-connection concurrency for streaming: 4-8 concurrent streams to balance latency vs throughput.

5) Telemetry hooks we recommend (these make troubleshooting much faster):
- log: request_id, model, prompt_token_count, response_token_count, status_code, latency_ms
- increment counters for 429/5xx and surface in SLO dashboards

Attachments: sparkbridge-sdk-quickstart.pdf, sparkbridge-mutual-action-plan.xlsx
Links: integration drive link in the spreadsheet.

Next steps: can we confirm sandbox creds and a kickoff slot (30–45m) next week? I cc'd Monica and Vivek to coordinate delivery tasks.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

Redwood Inference

Hi Parker — quick answers below and next steps. Mina from Security is looped for the SOC2 delivery.

1) Rate ceiling: hosted tiers are rate-fenced by default (50 req/s nominal with short bursts). For predictable 500 req/s spikes we recommend Dedicated — we can provision reserved capacity for bursts or set a dedicated pool. I'll open an internal provisioning ticket right after this thread.

2) Token limits & latency: for ~1k token payloads you will want to:
- Use streaming responses and hydrate UI progressively. Streaming latency is typically lower because you don't wait for full decode.
- Batch prompts where you can (e.g., 4 smaller prompts in one multipart request) — the server can process them in a single pass and usually results in lower per-prompt latency vs sequential calls.
- Set `max_output_tokens` conservatively and paginate long outputs.

3) SOC2 & compliance: attaching a summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf) — for the attestation we will provide a secure share. Mina, can you confirm the Red-team contact for SOC2 evidence share?

Telemetry/ops follow-up: we'll include a sample token-bucket limiter in the PR and a sidecar example for burst smoothing. Monica: if you push the PR link I will review and add a short comment with recommended timeouts (10s/60s) and backoff policy.

Kickoff: Tue Nov 17, 10:00–10:30 PT works for our delivery team — Vanessa, can you confirm?

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
